chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: Count Basie's band and Joe Jones at the Famous Door
summary: He first saw Basie's band at the Rockland Palace in 1938 and met drummer Joe Jones in 1939, calling him the sparkplug.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I think Count Basie's band came to New York in 1937. Did you ever run into that band with Joe Jones in that band, when Joe Jones was playing drums there?

I ran into that band in 1939 -- in 1938, I saw the band at the Rockland Palace, that was the first time I'd seen Joe Turner, a tall, skinny guy shouting the blues, but I never was able to get -- because in fact, when I came to New York, I didn't know hardly anybody, other than a

few musicians that had played around Miami. So I was sort of shy to go up to the bandstand and introduce myself; and furthermore, there were so many people around the guys in the band, I wouldn't have gotten the chance to speak to them anyway.

But I did get a chance to meet Joe in 1939 at the Famous Door when I was playing with Roy --I had just joined Roy, and Coleman Hawkins had just come in town from Europe, and we all went over to the Famous Door to see him, and that was when I met Joe Jones.
Oh, you never saw him play with the band, then?
I saw him play with the band at the Famous Door.
Yeah, in 1939. He was still with the band then.
And I was very much impressed with him because he was such a showman. Plus, I mean, he really made that band play. He was the sparkplug.
He really set it up, huh.
And I think he's still known as the world's greatest rhythm section.
Count Basie, Freddie Green, and Joe Jones. The most famous one, anyway.
